body:
We used an offline VM running a copy of our Agie Classic Cut 2S machine control. We imported CAMCraft’s 38-face die opening. The control plotted the inward offsets on every face, cut the 1 mm separation and completed three full trims. FORMALCHECK reported zero job errors.

All controller runs were offline. No physical cut was made.

Port onto the current frame, head `30e6c4c3f`. The branch takes a merge of #2968 (`1962fd5dc`). There is no rebase and no force-push. The die now uses the zero-step setup of #2984 through `PunchSetup20::encode_die`. That setup differs from the control-checked punch setup only in `ID_PUNCH,c_die`. The retired `jescript.rs` writer stays deleted. The die opening is reversed to clockwise. Thus the envelope, reach and spacing checks of #2968 offset toward the waste inside the opening. Each opening corner is an inside corner of the plate. The entry rules for a die are in `crates/post/src/agie/contour/entry.rs`. The 20 mm rule stays. The quick gate is green, except the known `crates/gpu/src/cut.rs:126` clippy finding. The offline control import of the zero-step `DIE20` job is still open. The PR body gives the steps.

## Offline control import: DIE20 (2026-11-23)

The job came from head `30e6c4c3f`, the head of this PR. The CLI ran `examples/agie/die-plate.camscript` without changes. The receipt says `"working_steps_generated": false`. The review text adds the c_die, inward-offset and slug-support checks.

### Procedure

- Emulated AGIEVISION CUT Classic S. A throwaway clone of the saved state `practice-color-ready`.
- Import of `DIE20.ISO`, then `DIE20.SBL` with its SBR, from a read-only floppy image. A host-side read of the guest disk confirmed that the imported ISO and SBL bytes are equal to the CamCraft files.
- New piece from `Script Files`. FORMALCHECK with and without warnings. TECCUT assignment. GRAFICHECK. The plot file `1.J00` was copied out and read.
- A second import from the same saved state was used only to read the `Startpunt`, `Geometrie` and `Inloop` pages of the work.

### Readings

| Reading | DIE20 |
|---|---|
| Work line after import | `CUT1 - CCB030[0], stp1,DIE20.ISO:1,` |
| Work page `Bewerking` | quality CCB030, wire `Berco Cut 0.25`, `Tec hoogte` 20.000 |
| Work page `Geometrie` | `Matrijs` selected (not `Stempel`), `Afkortsnede` 1.0, `DIE20.ISO:1`, closed contour, counter-clockwise |
| Work page `Startpunt` | `stp1`, X -5.500, Y 0.000, diameter 2.0 |
| Work page `Inloop` | perpendicular at the start of the element, 3.0 mm lead |
| FORMALCHECK before TECCUT | one error: `Technologie : te definiëren` (expected for zero steps) |
| TECCUT header | `M:x123 Mat:Fe Maf:BC TYPE:V Dia:0.25 H:20 Ra:0.30 Tkm:1.0 Te:1.5` |
| Pre-selected row | `0199 01.36 4`, technology `estbca25nnn060b030020` |
| Work line after TECCUT | `CCB030[4]` (Main, Trim1, Trim2, Trim3) |
| Pass offsets (µm) | 245, 155, 140, 134 |
| FORMALCHECK after TECCUT | `Controleresultaat: geen fouten.` |
| Warnings after TECCUT | `Uitgekozen opties : 131072`, `Referentiewaarden : te definiëren` |

The TECCUT header agrees with the receipt: steel (Fe), Berco Cut 0.25, 20 mm, CCB030 with Ra 0.30, Tkm 1.00 and Te 1.50.

### Plot (`1.J00`)

- Stock outline X-35 Y-35 to X35 Y35. Start hole X-5.5 Y0, diameter 2.0.
- The nominal entry is X-12.5 Y0 on the left wall. All offsets are inside the opening, toward the waste: the left wall is at X-12.255 (Main), -12.345 (Trim1), -12.360 (Trim2) and -12.366 (Trim3). At the bottom of the opening the values are Y-18.2541, -18.3444, -18.3595 and -18.3655.
- Each pass has the 38 faces of the opening. The opening corners are sharp (inside corners of the retained plate).
- The main loop stops at X-12.255 Y1.000 and leaves a 1.000 mm separation on the left wall.
- The separation section then cuts the 1 mm with the rough pass only.
- After the separation, Trim1, Trim2 and Trim3 each make one full loop of the opening. Each trim starts and ends at X-5.5 Y0.
- The slug is free after the separation section and before the trims. The operator must support it there, as the review text says.

### Result

DIE20 agrees with the expectation: zero steps at import, the c_die side (`Matrijs`), the ISO `DIE20.ISO`, the start hole X-5.5 Y0 d2.0, steel, Berco Cut 0.25, 20 mm, CCB030, the inward offsets 0.245, 0.155, 0.140 and 0.134 mm, no FORMALCHECK error after TECCUT, the entry at X-12.5 Y0, the 1 mm separation and three trims. I found no mismatch.

### Not checked

- No physical cut. The slug support was not simulated.
- Screenshots and the `.J00` file are in the local notes folder `agie-imports-20261123/DIE20`.

Needs changes before merge. Set `needs-rework` and `conflicts` for the two items below.

This is a SAFETY-tier review. I read the complete diff, including the parent stack. The die side, inward entry, prism proof and height refusals have pinning tests. The process line is present. This PR changes no UI code or snapshot PNG.

Requested before merge:

1. **P3 — control verification instructions:** `docs/user-guide/agie-wire-edm.md:60` gives the 20 mm offsets for every supported height. Step 1 now includes 40 and 80 mm. For 40 mm, the table and encoder require 0.260, 0.170, 0.140 and 0.130 mm. For 80 mm, they require 0.266, 0.176, 0.143 and 0.133 mm. The current instruction can make an operator accept the wrong technology or reject the correct technology. Replace the fixed list with a rule that selects the table row for the actual stock height. Apply that rule to the complete control-check procedure.
2. **Merge conflict:** `crates/post/src/agie_setup.rs:35` conflicts with current main `074c23ba675c2db3195ca3728155841d6b4e3c06`. Main added the inspection and publication modules beside the new offset table. `git merge-tree --write-tree <head> upstream/main` reports this file. Merge main into the branch. Keep both features and run the gate on the resolved head. Do not rebase or force-push.

Local build and tests:

The tested trial merge is `8e2231c9d3eda67a1293e7f6559ccb7912411d34`. Its first parent is this PR head. Its main parent is `7868d378680b325246b0dcdcdbf76c421f801cd9`. All commands ran locally in `.claude/worktrees/review-2969`. No GitHub runner was used.

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` | PASS: 1,187 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled; 18.4 minutes. Includes builds, touched suites and clippy with `-D warnings`. |
| `cargo xtask gate light` | PASS: 6 steps, 11 light tests, 0 failed, 0 stalled; 8.2 minutes. |
| `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` | PASS: 98 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled; 32.0 minutes. Two registered known failures failed as expected and passed the gate checks. |

These results apply to the stated trial merge. Main advanced during the run. The conflict with current main has no build result.

Extra suites run:

- `camcraft-post --lib`: 120 passed. This includes the die and reentrant tests.
- `camcraft-post --test agie_safe_setup`: 8 passed. This reads the changed golden directory.
- `camcraft-app --test agie_native`: 16 passed. This reads the die and notched-punch fixtures and the die golden.
- `camcraft-app --test example_catalog`: 39 debug tests and 4 heavy tests passed.
- `camcraft-app --test example_catalog_adaptive`: 1 passed.
- `camcraft-app --test example_catalog_edge_work`: 1 passed.
- `camcraft-kernel --test step_agreement`: 29 passed.
- Kernel `machining_mesh`, `machining_mesh_bounds`, `machining_mesh_open`, `machining_mesh_parity`, `machining_mesh_redivide` and `machining_mesh_shortfalls`: passed.
- `camcraft-app --test feature_edge_g1_join`: 5 passed.

Input mutations:

I ran the valid die example through the CLI. It returned success and published the job. I then repeated five mutations from the PR tests: outer rim, start in retained steel, incomplete rim, blind floor and unsupported stock height. Each returned an error and created no job directory. Thus the valid input was green and all five invalid inputs were red as expected. I changed no source code.

Goldens:

No existing golden or recorded NC/CL program moved. I checked all 78 lines of the new `DIE20.SBL` against `CCSEP20.SBL`. The differences are the stem, stock bounds, start-hole coordinates and `ID_PUNCH,c_die`. The setup and app suites confirm the bytes.

Notes:

- The [new offline control record](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/2969#issuecomment-7115465528) names this exact head. It reports zero steps on import, inward offsets, the separation, three trims and no FORMALCHECK error after TECCUT. I read this evidence. I did not run the control or make a physical cut.
- The reported GPU clippy failure did not recur on the tested trial merge.
- The worktree and `review-2969` branch remain in place to keep the build warm.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

This PR goes back to draft. The branch takes the new #2968 head `6443d4f09`. That head contains `main` at `44e6a8269` (#3219) and the TECCUT guide fix. The merge resolves the conflict with `main` and the review items of `30e6c4c3f`. A gate runs on the new head before the PR is ready again.

Reply to the [review of `30e6c4c3f`](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/2969#issuecomment-7116425278). New head: `d3443eddc`.

1. **Control verification instructions.** Step 3 of the control check in `docs/user-guide/agie-wire-edm.md` now uses the row of the selected stock thickness in the QN2 offsets table, in the order rough, trim 1, trim 2, trim 3. The step says that the post review names the same four offsets, and that a die plate uses the 20 mm row. Step 1 says that a punch can be 15, 20, 40 or 80 mm and a die is 20 mm only. The die corner text names the 20 mm row for its 0.245 mm offset. No other step of the procedure gives a fixed offset list. The table agrees with `QN2_OFFSETS_UM` and `controller_review`.
2. **Merge conflict.** The branch merges the #2968 head `6443d4f09`, which contains `main` at `44e6a8269` (#3219). In `crates/post/src/agie_setup.rs` the two features stay: the `inspection` and `publish` modules of `main`, the QN2 table, `encode_die` and `ID_PUNCH,c_die`. The merge also keeps the die text and the reentrant text in the camcraft-mcp skill row. No rebase and no force-push. The new head merges cleanly with `main` at `940cc5d0e`.

Posted bytes: no file under `crates/post/tests/golden/agie-setup/` changed, and `agie_safe_setup` (8) and `agie_native` (16) pass. Thus `DIE20` and the punch jobs are the same bytes as at `30e6c4c3f`. The [DIE20 control result](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/2969#issuecomment-7115465528) applies to the new head, and the body links it.

Gate on `d3443eddc`: batch plan, 1189 steps, 1 failed (`rotary_verify`, the known red of `main`, #3774), 0 stalled. Clippy is clean. The body has the details.

Ready for a re-check.

This is a SAFETY-tier re-review. The die tests pass. The process line is present. The PR changes no UI code or snapshot PNG.

### Earlier findings

I checked the [author's reply](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/2969#issuecomment-7119627456) against the code.

1. **Fixed: control verification instructions.** Head `d3443eddc` selects the offset table row for the stock thickness. The procedure states that a die uses the 20 mm row. The table agrees with the encoder.
2. **Fixed: merge conflict.** The trial merge is clean. The inspection and publication modules remain beside the offset table and die encoder. GitHub reports `MERGEABLE`.

### Requested before merge

1. **NEW blocker — failing heavy test after newer main:** `crates/app/tests/flute_reach.rs:102`. Test `a_ten_mm_flute_names_its_cause_before_the_rapid_findings` counts 12 rapid findings. It expects three. The gate step and a separate exact rerun both fail. Check the changed rapid paths and restore a justified assertion. Do not change the count without checking the output.
2. **NEW blocker — failing heavy test after newer main:** `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_hsm.rs:79`. Test `the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean` reads 5,232 facets. Its Linux pin expects 6,228. The gate step and a separate exact rerun both fail before the path checks. Validate the new mesh and the downstream path readings. Restore a green suite before merge.

Both tests passed in this review's first trial merge against main `940cc5d0e`. Main then added the kernel update and ring planner changes. These failures appeared after the refresh to `cd0222d9c`. The earlier review could not see this newer main. The review does not establish which main change caused each failure. The required all-green result is absent.

 right: 3

I repeated four input mutations through the final CLI: outer rim, pierce in retained steel, incomplete rim and stock changed to 40 mm. Each returned exit 1 and created no job folder. The valid input returned exit 0 and published the job.

Reply to the re-review of d3443eddc (the two new heavy blockers).

Both tests fail on main without this PR. I ran each one on main `cd0222d9c` (the second parent of your trial merge), in release, with `--ignored --exact`:

- `flute_reach::a_ten_mm_flute_names_its_cause_before_the_rapid_findings`: FAILED at `crates/app/tests/flute_reach.rs:102:5`, `left: 12`, `right: 3`. These are the same values as in your review. Main tracks this as #3811. The bisect there names #3790 as the first bad merge. The fix is PR #3827.
- `pocket3d_hsm::the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean`: FAILED on main. My run is on macOS aarch64, so it stops at the macOS pin (`crates/app/tests/pocket3d_hsm.rs:157`). Your Linux run stops at the Linux pin (line 79, 5232 against 6228). I found no open issue for this red on main. Please file it, because I cannot set the labels.

This PR changes only the wire EDM post, its setup writer, the die checks, the guide and the skill row. It does not change motion, kernel, the mesh readers or the milling checks. Thus these two failures do not come from this PR.

AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review" (#3556) also says that no PR gets the full heavy lanes, and that a heavy result is not a condition for ready or for a merge. This PR is P6, not a P1 under the safety floor.

The head is unchanged at d3443eddc. Ready for a re-check.
